data.name: Jedon
data.long_meaning: Jedon is a Hebrew name derived from the Hebrew word ‘Yadon’, meaning ‘hand’ or ‘God’s hand’. It symbolizes the belief that God is present and in control of every situation in one’s life. In the Bible, Jedidiah is a name given to a son born to King David after his sin with Bathsheba, symbolizing God's forgiveness and the restoration of David’s lineage. In Christian tradition, Jedon can be seen as a reminder of God's love, protection, and sovereignty.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies God's presence and control in one's life.

in_hebrew.name: ידעון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ידעון מקורו בשורש ידע, שפירושו לדעת או להכיר. הוא מופיע בתנ"ך כדמות ששמה קשור לידיעת האל או להבנת רצונו. השם נושא משמעות של קשר עם האל ועם הידע האלוהי.

in_greek.name: Ιεδων
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιεδων προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή λέξη 'ידעון' (Jideon) που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός γνωρίζει' ή 'γνωστός του Θεού'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόλο που δεν εμφανίζεται άμεσα, η έννοια της γνώσης και της αναγνώρισης του Θεού είναι κεντρική. Το όνομα εκφράζει τη σχέση του Θεού με τον άνθρωπο και την αποκάλυψη του Θείου.

in_latin.name: Jedon
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Jedon originem habet in voce hebrea 'ידעון' (Jedon), quae significat 'Deus scit' vel 'Deus cognoscit'. In traditione christiana, nomen hoc refert ad cognitionem et scientiam Dei. Est nomen quod connexionem divinam et revelationem Dei emphasizat.

in_english.name: Jedon
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jedon is derived from the Hebrew root 'ידע' (y-d-' ), meaning 'to know'. It conveys the idea that 'God knows' or 'known by God'. While not directly mentioned in the Bible, the concept is central to Christian theology, emphasizing a personal relationship with God and divine knowledge. Historically, it reflects the Judeo-Christian understanding of God as omniscient. The name Jedon symbolizes spiritual insight and divine connection.

historical_references.reference: Jedidiah (Jedon) was a son of King David and his wife Bathsheba. He is best known in the Bible as the person for whom the prophet Nathan made the famous promise: 'And your name shall not be so any more called Ariel, but the LORD that is over Israel shall be your God. This is what the LORD hath spoken, And Jedidiah, or rather a son shall be born unto thee, and thou shalt call his name JEDIDIAH, or elect of the LORD.' (2 Samuel 12:24-25, KJV)

'Jedon, Jedouin, or Jethon, a city of the tribe of Judah, six miles from Jerusalem, on the road to the south, and on the border of the wilderness of Judah. Nehemiah, when he came to Jerusalem from the king of Persia, found the city broken down and its gates burned with fire. He built the wall of Jerusalem, and the surrounding towns, and among them was JEDON. (Nehemiah 11:35, KJV)
